title: Finland becomes the 31st member of NATO
body:
Finland became NATO's 31st member on 4 April 2023, when Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto deposited the country's instrument of accession with the United States at NATO Headquarters in Brussels. U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken represented the United States as the treaty depositary.

NATO allies had signed Finland's Accession Protocol on 5 July 2022, after which all 30 national parliaments ratified the membership. Finnish President Sauli Niinisto attended a flag-raising ceremony at NATO Headquarters, the first time the Finnish flag was raised there. Flags were also raised simultaneously at the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe in Mons, Belgium, and at Allied Command Transformation in Norfolk, Virginia. Sweden, which had applied alongside Finland and was then still waiting for ratification, was represented at the ceremony by its foreign minister.

NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said: "We welcome Finland to the Alliance!" and added that "Finland is safer and NATO is stronger with Finland as an Ally." The accession followed Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, which led Finland to abandon its long-standing policy of military non-alignment. Finland's membership added a long land border with Russia to the alliance's frontier.
